Household impact examples: the household API's answers (net income before and after, by programme, by measure and the earnings sweep, with the marginal rate's parts by programme and net income's parts by programme at each sweep point) for the eight example households, each with every answer fixed in src/utils/exampleAnswers.js (no form default or prefill; rent £975 a month) and all nine candidate Autumn Budget 2026 measures selected (candidates modelled before the Budget, not announced policy), for 2027-28 to 2031-32. Regenerated on 26 October on Modal from main's code after #135 (scripts/precompute_household_presets.py's calculation, one container per entry) on policyengine 6.10.2 (policyengine-uk 2.132.6): every net income identical to the previous file; the sweep gains marginal_rate_parts; notes follow main's API wording; 17 own-point marginal rates move by 0.0001 (rounding). Hypothetical households; no survey records, ids or weights. On 26 October an eighth example, a lone parent working part time (lone-parent: one child aged 4, £14,000, renting, Universal Credit, £205 a month of childcare), was added: its five entries were calculated on Modal from main's code (5ee4e23e, #104) with the same calculation, and appended; the other 35 entries are byte-identical to the file Vahid signed (746f4e30). To regenerate on Budget day; pending review. On 26 October each example was given its own electricity, petrol and diesel spending, the average for its tenth of households by gross income (ONS Family Spending FYE 2025, Table A6; the driver keeps its own petrol), and all 40 entries were regenerated on the Modal test household app (uk-budget-household-test, build f32e8e76) with the same calculation; pending review. Reviewed and signed by Vahid Ahmadi on 26 October 2026, covering these bytes.

Percentiles (1st to 99th) of equivalised household net income, person-weighted, before and after each measure and the combined run, by year (2026-2031), from generate --only income_distribution --backend modal on the bundle's Microcosm UK 2024-25 dataset (policyengine 6.10.2, policyengine-uk 2.132.6). Income is household net income as the household calculator counts it (household_net_income less public spending in kind on the NHS, schools and transport subsidies, plus the business rates and stamp duty the model attributes to households), divided by the HBAI modified OECD scale; it differs from HBAI income (the decile charts and the Pre-measures forecast's median) mainly by including fuel duty and VAT. Each side is ranked against its own distribution. Each point is the mean income of the people in a band one percentile wide, never one household's figure; a band with fewer than 100 survey households has no row (none was dropped). No ids, weights or counts. No area below the UK. On the nine candidate Autumn Budget 2026 measures and their combined run (candidates modelled before the Budget, not announced policy). Every row is new and awaits review; read by the Household impact tab's 'Where you sit in the UK income distribution' card. Reviewed and signed by Vahid Ahmadi on 26 October 2026, covering these bytes. Regenerated on 26 October at 0fc752f3 (generate --only income_distribution --backend modal), after #187 (zero VAT on electricity in Great Britain only); reviewed again.
